bibl.title: The Pharos of Alexandria: A Man-Made "Mountain" in Lucan's Bellum Ciuile.
bibl.seg: Laura Zientek, The Pharos of Alexandria: A Man-Made "Mountain" in Lucan's Bellum Ciuile.
bibl.note: At Bellum Ciuile 8.463, Lucan describes the lighthouse of Alexandria as a mountain (mons). The Pharos is "mountainous" in height and of monumental significance as a man-made structure. Comparison with the Pyramids and its fiery illumination give the Pharos a funerary context and, due to its "mountainous" form and flames, also evoke the image of a volcano. The lighthouse contributes to the narrative of civil war with the ambiguity of its threat.
